It's a very interesting business model:

  • Browser blocks all website ads and tracking cookies, some of which may be carrying malware.
  • It instead serves its own ads, which have been vetted to be non-malware-carrying.
  • The revenue earned from these ads is shared between the browser maker, the website operator, and the browser user, in the form of credits.
  • The browser user can then use these credits to go ad-free on certain websites.

So this is a way to provide revenue to sites without risking malware infection and extensive user tracking.
